exams.name: UP TET
exams.fullName: Uttar Pradesh Teacher Eligibility Test
exams.body: Uttar Pradesh Basic Education Board / Examination Regulatory Authority, UP
exams.qualification: Paper I (classes I-V): Senior Secondary with D.El.Ed/BTC or equivalent. Paper II (classes VI-VIII): graduation with B.Ed/D.El.Ed as per NCTE norms. Refer official notification.
exams.ageLimit: No specific upper age limit for the eligibility test; recruitment posts have separate age criteria.
stages: Paper I and/or Paper II (objective offline exam)
exams.pattern: Each paper: 150 MCQs, 150 marks, 2.5 hours. Paper I: CDP, Language I (Hindi), Language II, Maths, EVS. Paper II: CDP, languages, and Maths-Science or Social Science. No negative marking.
exams.fee: Refer official notification (category-wise fee for one or both papers).
exams.vacancyRange: Eligibility certificate only; lakhs of candidates appear per cycle.
exams.salary: Not applicable (eligibility test; salary depends on subsequent UP teacher recruitment)
exams.detail: UP TET certifies eligibility to teach in Uttar Pradesh government and aided schools at primary (Paper I) and upper-primary (Paper II) levels. Qualifying is mandatory before applying for UP teacher recruitment drives.
prepTips: Prepare Hindi as Language I thoroughly since it carries significant weight for most candidates
Focus on Child Development and Pedagogy which is common to both papers and highly scoring
Solve previous UP TET papers to get used to the state-specific question style
Cover UP-specific general awareness and NCERT-aligned content for the concerned classes

exams.name: JEE Main
exams.fullName: Joint Entrance Examination (Main)
exams.qualification: Passed or appearing in Class 12 (or equivalent) with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics. For NIT/IIIT/CFTI admission, minimum board marks/percentile norms apply.
exams.ageLimit: No age limit to appear; candidates who passed Class 12 in the last two years or are appearing are eligible (year-based eligibility). Refer official notification.
exams.pattern: Paper 1 (B.E./B.Tech): Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics as MCQs and numerical questions, 300 marks, 3 hours, with negative marking. Best of two sessions is considered. Separate papers exist for B.Arch/B.Planning.
exams.fee: Refer official notification (category-wise application fee).
exams.vacancyRange: Entrance to NITs, IIITs, CFTIs and a gateway to JEE Advanced; over a million candidates appear.
exams.salary: Not applicable (entrance exam)
exams.detail: JEE Main is the national engineering entrance for admission to NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded technical institutions, and is the qualifying stage for JEE Advanced (for IIT admission). It is held in two sessions with the best score considered.
prepTips: Build conceptual clarity from NCERT first, then move to standard reference books for problem depth
Practise timed full-length mocks to master the computer-based test and manage negative marking
Maintain a formula and error log, revising it regularly before each session
Analyse each mock to fix weak chapters rather than only chasing new problems

exams.name: GATE
exams.fullName: Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering
exams.body: IISc and IITs (organising institute rotates annually)
exams.qualification: Bachelor's degree in Engineering/Technology/Architecture/Science or equivalent, or students in the final/pre-final year of such programmes as per eligibility norms.
exams.ageLimit: No age limit prescribed for GATE.
exams.pattern: One 3-hour computer-based paper of 100 marks comprising General Aptitude and the chosen subject, with MCQs, MSQs and numerical answer type questions. Negative marking applies to MCQs. Refer official notification.
syllabusOutline: Core subject syllabus of the chosen GATE paper
exams.fee: Refer official notification (category-wise and deadline-based fee).
exams.vacancyRange: Gateway to M.Tech/PhD admissions and many PSU recruitments; lakhs appear each year.
exams.salary: Not applicable (entrance/qualifying exam; PSU roles via GATE carry their own pay scales)
exams.detail: GATE tests comprehensive understanding of undergraduate engineering/science subjects. The score is used for M.Tech and PhD admissions in IITs, IISc, NITs and for recruitment by many public sector undertakings (PSUs).
prepTips: Do not ignore General Aptitude and Engineering Mathematics, which together are highly scoring
Focus on core subject fundamentals and previous years' questions, which repeat conceptually
Practise numerical answer type questions since they have no negative marking
Take subject-wise and full-length mocks on the official interface to build speed

exams.name: UPSC ESE
exams.fullName: Engineering Services Examination
exams.qualification: Engineering degree in the relevant discipline (Civil, Mechanical, Electrical, or Electronics & Telecommunication).
exams.ageLimit: 21 to 30 years for General category as on 1 January of exam year; category relaxations apply.
exams.pattern: Prelims has Paper I General Studies and Engineering Aptitude (200 marks) and Paper II discipline-specific (300 marks), both objective. Mains has two conventional papers of the chosen discipline (300 marks each), followed by a 200-mark interview.
syllabusOutline: Discipline core subjects (Civil / Mechanical / Electrical / Electronics & Telecom)
Materials, standards and project management basics
Ethics and personality assessment in interview
exams.fee: Rs. 200 for General/OBC; SC/ST, PwBD and female candidates exempted.
exams.vacancyRange: Around 150-500 posts (varies yearly by discipline).
exams.salary: Group A engineering posts at Level 10 pay (Rs. 56,100 basic) plus allowances.
exams.detail: ESE recruits Group A engineers for central engineering services and departments such as Railways, CPWD, CWC, telecom and defence engineering cadres. It demands strong technical depth in the chosen discipline.
prepTips: Build strong conceptual clarity in core discipline subjects rather than rote learning
Practise conventional answer writing for Mains with neat diagrams and derivations
Cover General Studies and Engineering Aptitude with current-affairs of infrastructure and technology
Solve previous-year ESE and GATE questions of your branch for concept overlap
Revise formulas and standards periodically using a consolidated formula sheet

exams.name: UPSC Combined Geo-Scientist
exams.fullName: Combined Geo-Scientist Examination
exams.qualification: Master's degree in the relevant stream: Geology, Geophysics, Chemistry or Hydrogeology as specified for each post in the notification.
exams.ageLimit: 21 to 32 years for General category as on 1 January of exam year; category relaxations apply.
exams.pattern: Stage I Prelims is objective (General Studies plus stream subject). Stage II Mains is descriptive across three stream papers. Stage III is a personality test. Refer official notification for exact marks.
syllabusOutline: Geology / Geophysics / Chemistry / Hydrogeology core (stream dependent)
Applied and quantitative fundamentals of the stream
exams.fee: Rs. 200 for General/OBC; SC/ST, PwBD and female candidates exempted.
exams.vacancyRange: Refer official notification (varies yearly across streams).
exams.salary: Group A scientist posts at Level 10 pay (Rs. 56,100 basic) plus allowances.
exams.detail: The Combined Geo-Scientist Examination recruits geologists, geophysicists, chemists and hydrogeologists mainly for the Geological Survey of India and the Central Ground Water Board. Candidates apply for the stream matching their postgraduate specialisation.
prepTips: Identify your correct stream (Geologist, Geophysicist, Chemist or Hydrogeologist) and target its syllabus
Build depth in the stream subject from standard postgraduate references
Prepare General Studies for the objective Prelims screening
Practise descriptive answers with diagrams and derivations for Mains
Analyse previous-year stream papers to prioritise high-weight topics

exams.name: AFCAT
exams.fullName: Air Force Common Admission Test
exams.qualification: Graduate degree for Flying and Ground Duty (Non-Technical) branches; relevant engineering degree for Ground Duty (Technical) branch, with prescribed marks and subject requirements.
exams.ageLimit: Around 20 to 24 years for Flying branch and 20 to 26 years for Ground Duty branches as per the notification; upper limits vary by branch.
stages: AFCAT online examination (and EKT for technical)
exams.pattern: Online objective test covering General Awareness, Verbal Ability in English, Numerical Ability and Reasoning & Military Aptitude, with negative marking. Technical candidates also take the Engineering Knowledge Test (EKT).
exams.fee: Around Rs. 250 as AFCAT examination fee (not charged for NCC special entry candidates). Refer official notification.
exams.vacancyRange: A few hundred vacancies across branches (varies yearly).
exams.salary: Officers commissioned at Level 10 pay plus military service pay and flying/technical allowances.
exams.detail: AFCAT is the entry test for commissioned officer roles in the Indian Air Force across the Flying, Ground Duty Technical and Ground Duty Non-Technical branches. Selection combines the written test with the AFSB interview and stringent medical standards.
prepTips: Practise numerical ability and reasoning for speed since time is tight
Read current affairs and defence-related general awareness regularly
Technical candidates should revise core engineering subjects for the EKT
Prepare for the AFSB with mock psychological tests, group tasks and interviews
Solve previous-year AFCAT papers to master the question distribution

exams.name: NIFT
exams.fullName: National Institute of Fashion Technology Entrance Examination
exams.qualification: For B.Des/B.F.Tech: passed or appearing in Class 12. For M.Des/M.F.M/M.F.Tech: relevant bachelor's degree as per programme norms.
exams.ageLimit: Age limit may apply to undergraduate design programmes as per the notification; refer official notification.
stages: Creative Ability Test (CAT) and/or General Ability Test (GAT)
Situation Test / Group Discussion / Personal Interview (programme dependent)
exams.pattern: Written entrance combining Creative Ability Test (design aptitude and drawing) and General Ability Test (quantitative, communication, analytical, GK), followed by a situation test or interview depending on the programme. Refer official notification.
syllabusOutline: Creative Ability Test (design and drawing aptitude)
exams.fee: Refer official notification (category-wise fee).
exams.vacancyRange: Entrance to NIFT campuses across India for design, technology and management programmes.
exams.salary: Not applicable (entrance exam)
exams.detail: The NIFT entrance examination admits students to Bachelor's and Master's programmes in design, fashion technology and fashion management across NIFT campuses. Design programmes involve a creative test and situation test in addition to the written exam.
prepTips: Build a daily sketching and design-thinking habit for the Creative Ability Test
Prepare quantitative, analytical and English sections for the General Ability Test
Follow fashion, design and general current affairs for the GK component
For the situation test, practise model-making and material handling within time limits

exams.name: UPSC Geologist
exams.fullName: Combined Geo-Scientist Examination (Geologist stream)
exams.qualification: Master's degree in Geology or Applied Geology or an equivalent qualification specified in the notification.
exams.ageLimit: 21 to 32 years for General category as on 1 January of exam year; category relaxations apply.
exams.pattern: Prelims has objective papers on General Studies and Geology. Mains has descriptive Geology papers, followed by a personality test. Marks scheme varies; refer official notification.
exams.fee: Rs. 200 for General/OBC; SC/ST, PwBD and female candidates exempted.
exams.vacancyRange: Refer official notification (varies yearly).
exams.salary: Group A scientist post at Level 10 pay (Rs. 56,100 basic) plus allowances.
exams.detail: The Geologist stream of the Combined Geo-Scientist Examination recruits geologists mainly for the Geological Survey of India. It requires strong postgraduate-level geology knowledge.
prepTips: Revise core geology subjects from standard postgraduate texts systematically
Practise diagram-based descriptive answers for the Mains stage
Prepare General Studies and current affairs for the Prelims screening
Solve previous-year Geo-Scientist papers to identify recurring themes
Use flashcards for mineral properties, rock types and stratigraphic sequences

exams.name: RRB NTPC
exams.fullName: Railway Recruitment Board Non-Technical Popular Categories
exams.qualification: Class 12 (10+2) for undergraduate-level posts and a graduate degree for graduate-level posts, depending on the category applied for.
exams.ageLimit: Broadly 18 to 33/36 years depending on post level as on the notification's cut-off date; category relaxations apply.
exams.pattern: Objective CBT 1 (100 questions) is a screening stage, followed by a more detailed CBT 2. Both cover Mathematics, General Intelligence & Reasoning, and General Awareness, with negative marking of one-third.
syllabusOutline: Mathematics (arithmetic, number system, percentages, ratio, time and work)
exams.fee: Around Rs. 500 for General/OBC (largely refunded on appearing); Rs. 250 for reserved categories (refundable). Refer official notification.
exams.vacancyRange: Several thousand posts nationwide (varies yearly).
exams.frequency: Released as and when vacancies arise
exams.salary: Level 2 to Level 6 pay depending on post (Rs. 19,900 to Rs. 35,400 basic) plus allowances.
exams.detail: RRB NTPC recruits for non-technical posts such as clerk, typist, station master, goods guard and junior accounts assistant. Applications are made region-wise through the respective Railway Recruitment Board websites, so candidates should apply via the RRB region of their choice.
prepTips: Master arithmetic shortcuts to solve the maths section quickly and accurately
Practise reasoning puzzles, series and coding-decoding daily
Revise static GK and follow last 6-12 months of current affairs
Take sectional and full-length mock tests to build CBT speed
For typist and skill-test posts, practise typing on a keyboard regularly

exams.name: Bihar STET
exams.fullName: Bihar Secondary Teacher Eligibility Test
exams.qualification: Paper I (secondary, classes 9-10): relevant PG/graduation with B.Ed as per subject. Paper II (senior secondary, classes 11-12): relevant post-graduation with B.Ed. Refer official notification.
exams.ageLimit: Minimum 21 years; upper age limit as per Bihar government norms with category-wise relaxations. Refer official notification.
stages: Paper I and/or Paper II (computer-based objective test)
exams.pattern: Each paper: 150 objective questions, 150 marks. Contains subject-specific questions plus teaching aptitude/pedagogy and general components. Refer official notification for exact split.
syllabusOutline: Subject-specific content for the concerned subject
exams.fee: Refer official notification (separate fee for one or both papers, category-wise).
exams.vacancyRange: Eligibility certificate only; large number of candidates appear per cycle.
exams.salary: Not applicable (eligibility test; salary depends on subsequent Bihar teacher recruitment)
exams.detail: Bihar STET certifies eligibility to teach at secondary (Paper I) and senior secondary (Paper II) levels in Bihar. Qualifying is a prerequisite for secondary teacher recruitment conducted by the Bihar authorities.
prepTips: Prioritise deep subject mastery as the majority of marks come from subject-specific questions
Cover teaching methodology and pedagogy for the secondary/senior-secondary level
Add Bihar-focused general knowledge and current affairs to your daily revision
Practise the CBT interface with mock tests to build speed and accuracy

exams.name: LIC AAO
exams.fullName: Life Insurance Corporation of India Assistant Administrative Officer
exams.qualification: Bachelor's/Master's degree from a recognised university; relevant qualification for specialist AAO posts.
exams.ageLimit: 21-30 years; standard relaxations apply for reserved categories.
exams.pattern: Prelims: reasoning, quantitative aptitude and English. Mains: reasoning, general knowledge & current affairs, data analysis & interpretation, insurance & financial market awareness, plus English descriptive, followed by an interview.
exams.fee: Refer official notification (concessional fee for SC/ST/PwD).
exams.vacancyRange: Varies yearly (typically several hundred).
exams.salary: Approx Rs 53,600 basic (AAO scale) with allowances.
exams.detail: LIC AAO recruits Assistant Administrative Officers for the Life Insurance Corporation of India in generalist and specialist streams such as IT, actuarial, CA and legal.
prepTips: Build strong insurance and financial market awareness for the Mains section
Practise data interpretation and reasoning puzzles at a high difficulty level
Prepare English descriptive writing on economy and insurance themes
For specialist posts, revise your professional subject alongside the common sections

exams.name: SBI SO
exams.fullName: State Bank of India Specialist Officer / Specialist Cadre Officer
exams.qualification: Relevant professional qualification and work experience as specified for each specialist post.
exams.ageLimit: Varies by post (commonly 21-40 years); standard relaxations apply.
exams.pattern: Selection is typically through an online written test on professional knowledge plus aptitude, or shortlisting on experience, followed by an interview; process varies by advertisement.
exams.fee: Refer official notification (fee exemption for SC/ST/PwD).
exams.vacancyRange: Varies yearly by specialist post.
exams.salary: Varies by post and scale; officer scales as per SBI structure.
exams.detail: SBI SO recruits Specialist Cadre Officers in areas such as IT, risk, credit, law and marketing through periodic advertisements with varying selection processes.
prepTips: Read each specific advertisement carefully as eligibility and process differ per post
Focus preparation on domain/professional knowledge for your specialisation
Update your resume with clearly quantified relevant work experience
Prepare for a technical interview covering practical scenarios in your field

exams.name: RRB ALP
exams.fullName: Railway Recruitment Board Assistant Loco Pilot
exams.qualification: Class 10 pass plus ITI in a relevant trade, or a diploma/degree in a relevant engineering discipline.
exams.ageLimit: Broadly 18 to 33 years as on the notification's cut-off date; category relaxations apply.
stages: CBT 2 (with part A and part B)
exams.pattern: CBT 1 is a screening objective test. CBT 2 has Part A (maths, reasoning, general awareness) and Part B (trade-related, qualifying). Qualified candidates take the Computer Based Aptitude Test, which requires stringent medical fitness.
exams.fee: Around Rs. 500 for General/OBC (largely refunded on appearing); Rs. 250 for reserved categories (refundable). Refer official notification.
exams.vacancyRange: Several thousand posts nationwide (varies yearly).
exams.frequency: Released as and when vacancies arise
exams.salary: Level 2 pay (Rs. 19,900 basic) plus running and other allowances.
exams.detail: RRB ALP recruits Assistant Loco Pilots who operate locomotives. Selection includes two CBTs, a qualifying trade test, a driving aptitude test and strict medical standards (especially vision). Applications are region-wise via the respective RRB websites.
prepTips: Prepare Part B trade/engineering topics as per your ITI or diploma discipline
Practise the driving aptitude test formats separately since it is decisive
Ensure your vision meets the A1 medical standard before investing heavily
Build speed in maths, reasoning and general science for the CBTs
Solve previous-year ALP papers to understand part A and part B balance

exams.name: MPPSC
exams.fullName: Madhya Pradesh Public Service Commission State Service Examination
exams.qualification: Bachelor's degree in any discipline from a recognised university.
exams.ageLimit: Generally 21 to 40 years with category and MP-domicile relaxations. Refer official notification.
exams.pattern: Prelims: two objective papers (General Studies and General Aptitude/CSAT). Mains: six descriptive papers including General Studies, Hindi and essay. Followed by interview. Refer official notification.
syllabusOutline: General Studies (history, geography, polity, economy, science)
Madhya Pradesh-specific GK, history and culture
exams.fee: Refer official notification (category-wise application fee).
exams.vacancyRange: Typically a few hundred posts per cycle across state services.
exams.salary: As per Madhya Pradesh government pay levels for Deputy Collector/DSP and allied posts. Refer official notification.
exams.detail: MPPSC State Service Examination recruits for Madhya Pradesh administrative and allied Group A and B posts including Deputy Collector and DSP. Madhya Pradesh general knowledge forms a substantial part of the syllabus.
prepTips: Dedicate significant time to Madhya Pradesh static GK, culture, geography and schemes
Prepare Hindi and essay writing which carry weight in the Mains
Solve MPPSC prelims PYQs to understand the heavy MP-GK focus
Maintain concise current-affairs notes blending national and state news

exams.fee: Refer official notification (examination fee as applicable).
exams.vacancyRange: Several thousand Agniveer vacancies per intake (varies yearly).
exams.salary: Agniveer package under the Agnipath scheme with a monthly Agniveer package and Seva Nidhi on completion of the tenure.
exams.detail: The Indian Air Force enrols Agniveervayu under the Agnipath scheme for a fixed tenure across Science and Other-than-Science trades. Selection is through an online examination, physical fitness test and medical examination.
prepTips: For the Science stream, revise class 11-12 Physics and Maths thoroughly
Practise English and Reasoning & General Awareness for both streams
Build running stamina and strength for the physical fitness test
Confirm the eyesight and medical standards before applying
Take timed online mock tests to handle the exam interface confidently

Domain concepts of the chosen PG programme
exams.fee: Refer official notification (fee varies by number of papers and category).
exams.vacancyRange: Entrance to postgraduate programmes across central and participating universities; lakhs appear.

Revise your undergraduate core syllabus, which forms the basis of most questions
Solve subject-wise mocks to handle the MCQ format and negative marking
Keep track of participating-university-specific eligibility and cutoffs

exams.name: UPSC CDS
exams.fullName: Combined Defence Services Examination
exams.qualification: Bachelor's degree for IMA/OTA; Engineering degree for INA; degree with Physics and Mathematics (or engineering) for AFA. Requirements differ by academy.

SSB: officer intelligence, psychology, group tasks and interview

Read a newspaper daily and revise static GK from a standard yearbook
Improve English through grammar drills, vocabulary and reading comprehension practice
Prepare for the SSB separately with mock group discussions, psychological tests and self-description exercises
Maintain physical fitness early since medical and SSB stages test endurance

exams.name: MPSC
exams.fullName: Maharashtra Public Service Commission State Services Examination

exams.detail: MPSC State Services recruits for Maharashtra administrative and allied Group A and B posts including Deputy Collector and Deputy Superintendent of Police. It is the premier state civil services examination in Maharashtra.

Focus on Maharashtra-specific history, geography and current affairs
Practise CSAT to comfortably clear the qualifying aptitude paper
Use previous years' MPSC papers to align with the state-specific pattern

exams.name: NATA

exams.vacancyRange: Qualifying test for admission to B.Arch programmes across India.

exams.detail: NATA, conducted by the Council of Architecture, is the aptitude test for admission to the five-year Bachelor of Architecture (B.Arch) programme across institutions in India. It measures drawing, observational and reasoning aptitude relevant to architecture.

Strengthen mathematics and logical reasoning for the objective portions
Develop aesthetic sensitivity by observing buildings, forms and everyday design
Attempt multiple sessions strategically since the best score is typically considered

Keep up daily physical training to clear the medical and SSB physical standards

Follow recent current affairs and static GK from a reliable source
Train for the 1.6 km run, pull-ups and other physical standards well in advance
Verify height, chest and weight measurement standards for your region
Practise online mock CEE tests to build speed and accuracy

exams.name: NVS Teacher

Strengthen both English and Hindi language sections as both are commonly tested
